spans.s:
Stega in the Yajurveda Saṃhitās^1 seems to denote a species
of ‘worm.’ The word occurs in the Rigveda^2 also, where its
sense is unknown, but may possibly be ‘ploughshare.’^3
1) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 7, 11, 1;
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxv. 1.
2) x. 31, 9 = Av. xviii. 1, 39. Cf.
Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 98.
3) Weber, Proceedings of the Berlin
Academy, 1895, 833. Cf. Whitney,
Translation of the Atharvaveda, 824.

Stena is a common word for ‘thief’ from the Rigveda^1
onwards.^2 See
Steya denotes ‘theft’ in the Atharvaveda^1 and later.^2 Cf.

) xi. 8, 20; xiv. 1, 57.
2) Nirukta, vi. 27; Kauṣītaki Upani-
ṣad, iii. 1. Cf. steya-kṛt, ‘thief,’ in
